model: Owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods/references/owner-fcf.md) with section 7 cyclical adaptations: mid-cycle margin reversion, combined tax+NCI leakage, leases as debt, debt-like Samarco and streaming liabilities in the bridge, USD WACC, AUD quote
current_price_source: Yahoo Finance chart API BHP.AX regularMarketPrice

inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 5,081.4m BHP Group Limited ordinary shares on issue at the FY2026 report date (Annual Report p.2) plus 11m dilutive employee share awards (note 7). Held FLAT: employee share awards are expensed (US$123m FY2026) and funded by the Employee Equity Trust buying/issuing ~3-5m shares a year, so expensing and diluting would double-charge. No non-SBC issuance is expected; last on-market buy-back was FY2019 (US$5.2bn), none current.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bridge deduction US$18,150m = BHP-defined net debt US$8,694m (30-Jun-2026; borrowings 23,625 + leases 3,496 less 735 freight-index leases less cash 18,532 less net debt-management derivatives 840) + Samarco dam-failure provision US$5,197m (discounted, note 4; utilised US$2,030m in FY2026 via investing-line funding of Samarco, so it sits OUTSIDE reported FCF) + Antamina silver-stream liability US$4,259m (US$4,300m proceeds Jul-2025 less US$41m settled; BHP excludes it from net debt, but it is an upfront sale of future by-product cash that the projected flows still count through the equity-accounted Antamina profit share). Total debt 27,121 less cash 18,532 = 8,589 before derivatives/freight leases. Book NCI (US$5,398m) is NOT deducted: NCI is charged in the flows via the combined tax+NCI leakage rate (section 7c, charge once).
inputs.lease_treatment: A (leases as debt): lease liabilities sit in BHP net debt (ex freight-index vessel leases, which are operating-cost pass-throughs); lease principal is NOT deducted from flows; lease additions (US$1,111m FY2026) are folded into capex_pct so right-of-use renewal is charged as capex-like spend.
inputs.reported_fcf_definition: Net operating cash flows 21,778 less capital and exploration expenditure 10,257 (Metrics.csv basis). BHP's own 'free cash flow' (OCF less ALL investing = 9,767) additionally nets US$2,380m EAI funding (mostly Samarco settlement funding) and US$847m disposal proceeds.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report note 5 'Expenses excluding net finance costs' - Employee share awards US$123m (FY2025 127, FY2024 112). Not a cash-flow add-back line in BHP's format; no separate equity-award tax withholding is disclosed (awards are net-settled through the Employee Equity Trust).
inputs.interest_income_note: US$573m interest income (note 23) stripped from the owner-FCF anchor because the US$18.5bn cash pile is netted in the bridge; the component build starts from Underlying EBITDA, which already excludes it.
inputs.buyback_note: No on-market buy-back in FY2024-FY2026 (Directors' Report s.4). Flat count is a modelling convention funded by ~US$0.1bn/yr trust purchases, not a repurchase programme.
inputs.fx_rate_direction: AUD -> USD multiplier (AUDUSD=X): takes the ASX price to the USD of the financials; per-share values computed in USD and divided by this rate to reach AUD
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in USD (IFRS, Australian filer); ASX quote in AUD. All per-share values computed in USD then converted at AUD/USD 0.714 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-09-21T11:54:08Z). Parity check on the NYSE ADR (1 ADR = 2 ordinary shares): US$86.27 / 2 = US$43.13 vs A$60.78 x 0.714 = US$43.40, a 0.6% gap (ADR is the Friday 18-Sep close, ASX is Monday 21-Sep) - rate, direction and ADR ratio confirmed.
inputs.model_currency_note: currency=USD is the ISO code of the statements; quote_currency=AUD is the ISO code of the ASX price. intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry_price are in AUD (quote); *_usd twins carry the flow-currency figures.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built WACC: risk-free 4.2% (US 10y, Sep-2026), ERP 5.0%, beta 1.05 -> cost of equity 9.45%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.2% (BHP USD notes), tax 30% -> 3.6%; debt weight 11% (US$27bn gross debt vs ~US$220bn market cap) -> 8.8%, rounded to the house 9.0%. Cyclicality, China concentration and Samarco are charged in the scenario flows and weights, NOT as a WACC premium, and the same WACC is used in all three scenarios (section 7f, charge risk once).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, cyclical / non-US -> owner-fcf.md + section 7). Not a bank, REIT, LIC or holdco; BHP is an operating miner whose value is a stream of free cash flow, so the FCF engine applies, with the mid-cycle normalisation the memory precedents (SAN.NZ, 3116.T, 2CC.NZ) require for cyclicals. KEY CHOICES: (1) FY2026 is a margin peak (56.1% Underlying EBITDA margin on record copper) - the base fades margin to the 52% ten-year median and revenue by ~5% before volume growth resumes, rather than carrying FY2026 forward. (2) Tax and NCI are combined into one 'cash_tax_rate_path' leakage driver (~35% tax+royalty on EBIT and ~19.5-21% NCI on PAT -> 47.5-49%) so the flows are attributable-only; book NCI is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge. FY2026 calibration: Underlying EBIT 26,640 x (1-0.477) = 13,933 vs underlying attributable profit 13,204 + after-tax net finance cost ~445 = 13,649, a 2% tie. (3) Leases as debt (treatment A). (4) Samarco provision and the Antamina silver stream are deducted as debt-like claims because neither cash outflow passes through the projected flows. (5) Horizon 10 years because capex intensity and the Jansen/copper volume ramp are still moving until ~FY2032; terminal cap 15x owner FCF (top of the 12-15x cyclical band, justified by tier-1 cost position); the cap binds in bull, Gordon binds in bear and base at 9%/2.5% sits just under it. (6) Equity-accounted investments (Antamina, Samarco, Vicuna): BHP's Underlying EBITDA includes the profit share and OCF includes dividends received (US$895m FY2026); no adjustment. Vicuna growth funding is expected to run through the EAI investing line and is NOT explicitly in capex_pct - a known omission in the bull case. SBC-NEAR-ZERO: employee share awards are 0.2% of revenue so house and street bases nearly coincide; band_position is reported but is a degenerate measure here.

historical_growth.fcf_basis: owner FCF = reported FCF (OCF - capital & exploration) - employee share awards expense - interest income; SBC-adjusted series used for fcf_*_cagr
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base_case_10yr_revenue_cagr (volume-led: Escondida/Copper SA +900-1,000ktpa FY28-31, Jansen S1 FY28 and S2 FY31, WAIO >305Mt, plus ~2% inflation; price mean-reverting from FY2026 record copper)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every trailing CAGR here measures the commodity price cycle, not the business: the 5-year window starts at the FY2021 iron-ore/copper peak (revenue -0.7%/yr, equity -0.1%/yr) and the 3-year window starts at the FY2023 trough (revenue +3.0%/yr, equity +4.6%/yr). None is used as a forward growth rate; the forward path is built from volume guidance and a mid-cycle price reset.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (3y -0.5%, 5y -11.5%) sit below reported-FCF CAGRs (3y -0.3%, 5y -10.5%) only because interest income grew from US$73m (FY2021) to US$573m (FY2026) on a larger cash pile; SBC is flat at ~US$0.1bn/yr and is not a growing claim. 10-year average underlying attributable profit FY2017-FY2026 is US$12.5bn (FY2026: US$13.2bn), so FY2026 is above but not far above mid-cycle on earnings; on margin it is a peak (56.1% vs 52% ten-year median).

assumption_notes.growth_rates: Nominal revenue growth, % YoY, FY2027E-FY2036E. Base: -4/-1 (price reset) then 4.5-5 (Escondida growth program, Copper SA, Jansen S1 from FY2028, S2 from FY2031, WAIO >305Mt) tapering to 2.5.
assumption_notes.ebitda_margin_path: Underlying EBITDA margin (BHP definition, post-IFRS16, includes EAI profit share). Ten-year history: 40/53/54/52/51/61/62/52/52/51/56 (FY2016-FY2026); median 52%.
assumption_notes.sbc_pct_path: Employee share awards expense as % of revenue, flat at the FY2026 actual 0.2%.
assumption_notes.da_pct: D&A 11.0% of revenue (FY2026 10.6%, FY2024-25 9.5-10.8%; rises as the capex programme depreciates).
assumption_notes.capex_pct_path: Capital and exploration expenditure PLUS lease additions as % of revenue. FY2026: (10,257 + 1,111)/58,760 = 19.3%. BHP guides ~US$11bn/yr capex through the medium term; copper growth capex US$1.4bn FY2027, US$1.9bn FY2028, ~US$3bn/yr FY2029-31; Jansen S1 to FY2028, S2 to FY2031. Held near 20% then stepped down to sustaining + depletion replacement (~13.5%) by FY2036.
assumption_notes.wc_capture_pct: -10% of the change in revenue (receivables + inventory exceed payables: FY2026 working-capital build was US$1.4bn on a US$7.5bn revenue increase, -19%, but that increase was price-led; -10% assumed for the volume-led path).
assumption_notes.cash_tax_rate_path: COMBINED leakage on EBIT = 1 - (1 - tax) x (1 - NCI). Tax and royalty-related taxation 35% of EBIT (adjusted ETR 36.5% of PBT FY2026; statutory 41.9% incl. impairment); NCI 19.5% of underlying PAT in FY2026 rising to 21% (base) / 23% (bull) as the 42.5%-minority Escondida grows. Bear: 46% (lower copper profit reduces the NCI share).
assumption_notes.terminal_growth: Bear 2.0 / base 2.5 / bull 3.0%: long-run commodity prices flat in real terms plus 2-2.5% inflation, with volume depletion offset by sustaining capex in capex_pct_path.
assumption_notes.terminal_cap_multiple: 15x year-10 owner FCF. At 9%/2.5% Gordon = 15.8x so the cap binds by a hair in base; Gordon binds in bear (14.6x); cap binds in bull (Gordon 17.2x). Today's EV/owner-FCF (FY2026) is ~21x, so no exit multiple expansion is assumed in any scenario.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle reversion with volume growth. Copper fades from the FY2026 record toward a long-run ~US$4.25/lb and iron ore settles around US$90-95/t, so revenue slips ~5% over FY2027-28 even as volumes rise; from FY2029 the Escondida growth program, Copper SA, Jansen Stage 1 (first potash mid-CY2027 = FY2028) and Stage 2 (FY2031) plus WAIO >305Mt lift nominal revenue 4-5%/yr, tapering to 2.5%. Underlying EBITDA margin fades from 56.1% (FY2026) to the 52% ten-year median by FY2029 and stays there (Jansen's >65% margin is too small to move the group). Capex plus lease additions held at the US$11bn guidance run-rate (20% of revenue) through the Jansen/Escondida build, then declines to ~13.5% (sustaining plus depletion replacement) by FY2036. Tax+royalty at 35% of EBIT and NCI (42.5% of Escondida, Samarco-adjacent JV partners) at 19.5-21% of after-tax profit are combined into one 47.5-49% leakage driver that rises with copper mix. Samarco settlement (US$5.2bn provision, paid over 20 years), the US$4.3bn Antamina silver stream and BHP's own US$8.7bn net debt are deducted once in the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: Copper supercycle plus resilient China steel. Copper holds at or above US$5/lb on electrification, grid and AI data-centre demand; iron ore stays ~US$100/t because Chinese steel output has now exceeded 1bn t for six straight years; Jansen delivers on the revised schedule and the Escondida concentrator (230-270ktpa) is approved. Revenue grows 3-6%/yr through FY2032 with margins at 56-57%. Because copper (higher-NCI) drives the mix, the tax+NCI leakage rises to 50%. Same WACC as base: cyclicality is priced in the flows, not the discount rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: China steel peak, copper reset, and the liability tail bites. Iron ore falls to ~US$75/t as Chinese property-led steel demand finally rolls over (management has already been wrong-footed once on the timing), copper resets to ~US$3.75/lb as new supply (Anglo-Teck, Rio-Glencore scale, Kamoa, Oyu Tolgoi) arrives, and metallurgical coal stays weak. Revenue falls 15% in FY2027 and 6% in FY2028 before growing 2-3% on volume; margins compress to 46% (FY2016-style cost-curve pressure with AUD/CLP tailwinds partly offsetting). Capex cannot flex below ~US$11bn until Jansen S1/S2 and the copper program finish, so capex intensity peaks at 23% of revenue. The UK Samarco causation trial (Oct-2026 to Mar-2027) and a possible damages trial add unquantified cost beyond the US$5.2bn provision; Jansen Stage 2 shows a second overrun. Terminal growth 2%.

entry_price.method: Entry price = (sum FCF_t/1.15^t + TV_10@hurdle/1.15^10 - bridge) / shares, TV@hurdle = min(FCF_10 x (1+g)/(0.15-g), 15 x FCF_10), computed per scenario and probability-weighted; converted to AUD at the same rate as intrinsic value.
entry_price.note: With the 15x terminal cap re-applied at every rate, no discount rate above g+0.5pp reproduces A$60.78 in base or bull (null = cap-bound: the capped value tops out at A$60 base / A$75 bull even at 3-3.5%). On an uncapped Gordon terminal the price implies a 6.7% return in base and 8.2% in bull. The entry price sits near half of intrinsic value, which is what demanding 15% from flows the model discounts at 9% costs; it is not a bug.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_10)). The 9% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value; the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC 7-11%, columns = terminal growth 1.5-3.5% (base 2.5% +/- 1pp). Terminal value re-capped at 15x FCF_10 in every cell, which is why low-WACC / high-g cells flatten.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25% bear / 50% base / 25% bull, moved from the house 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25% because the FY2026 base year is a commodity-price peak (record copper, 56% margin) and mean reversion is the central risk for a price-taker, not a tail - management itself was wrong-footed on the last China steel call, and the Samarco UK causation trial (Oct-2026 to Mar-2027) is a dated, live liability catalyst. Bull cut to 25% because it needs two independent prices (copper AND iron ore) to hold near record simultaneously while Jansen and the Escondida concentrator execute on schedule. Balance sheet (13% gearing, US$18.5bn cash) rules out solvency-type bear weights above 25%.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-near-zero name: employee share awards are 0.2% of revenue, so the house/street band is only ~A$0.4 wide and band_position (price far above both) is a degenerate measure; the gap to price is the mid-cycle/discount-rate view, not SBC treatment.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House owner-FCF basis: SBC expensed, share count flat, NCI and tax charged in the flows, leases and debt-like provisions deducted once, mid-cycle margins, terminal value capped at 15x FCF. The gap to the market price is the price of (a) the market discounting a franked-dividend blue chip at ~6-7% rather than 9% and (b) copper staying at record levels; both are visible in the required-return table and bull case rather than being baked into the base.
valuation_philosophy.what_would_change_the_view: Evidence that copper >US$5/lb is the new mid-cycle (bull margin path), a lower USD risk-free rate, or resolution of the Samarco UK action inside the provision would move the weighted value toward the bull case; a China steel-demand roll-over or a second Jansen overrun toward the bear.

methodology.discounting: end-of-year, year 1 discounted one full period
methodology.entry_price: TV rebuilt at the 15% hurdle (2026-09-01 rule)
methodology.currency: USD flows, USD WACC, AUD quote via AUDUSD=X

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
